While there are a few drawbacks, such as limited color options and a strong initial odor, the overall performance of the dye is impressive. For those seeking a reliable product to enhance their facial hair appearance, this dye is definitely worth considering. Just remember to perform a patch test if you have sensitive skin! Yes Product description Product Description HG Mould Spray is a fast-acting black mould remover for walls and household surfaces affected by visible mould, mildew, fungus and algae in damp areas. Its targeted, self-acting spray has a bleaching action and works in around 30 minutes, helping remove stains without scrubbing on compatible surfaces. Use it indoors in bathrooms, showers, toilets, kitchens, cellars, basements and saunas on suitable plastered walls, tiles, grout, silicone joints, window frames and other compatible surfaces. It can also be used outdoors around compatible swimming pools, facades, balconies, plant boxes and garden ornaments, excluding wood. One 500ml bottle treats approximately 2–3 m² of wall surface or 6–8 m² of tile grout. Ensure good ventilation and wear suitable rubber or plastic gloves. Remove the safety clip or unlock the nozzle. Spray from approximately 3–5cm away and leave for 30 minutes. Clean the treated area with water and a sponge. For stubborn stains, reapply and leave for a further 30 minutes. For silicone joints, wash off after 30 minutes and repeat if necessary. Always test first in an inconspicuous area. Permanent brown discolouration may occur on elastic grouting, badly glazed tiles or old tiles with hairline cracks. Do not use on wood, coloured surfaces, ceilings, clothing, paintwork, plastic shower trays, vertical blinds, aluminium, stainless steel or other sensitive metals. Avoid splashes and do not reuse the bottle. Never mix with other cleaning products, as dangerous chlorine gas may be released. Wash hands after handling. Store and transport cool, dark and upright. Very toxic to aquatic life; avoid release into the environment. Keep out of reach of children and read the label before use. For very deep, dark, or large areas of mould that have penetrated the sealant, multiple applications may be necessary, but even then, the mould fades significantly. This product works wonders not just on bathroom and kitchen sealants but also on discoloured grout, window frames and seals, skirting boards, backs of furniture (with care—always test a small area first and avoid soaking expensive or varnished items), and bathroom/shower walls and ceilings. I recommend wearing a mask and goggles (especially if spraying higher areas like ceilings) and ensuring the room is well-ventilated by opening windows. With common-sense safety measures in place, it’s easy to use effectively. As someone who works in property management and deals with over 20 properties annually that have condensation-related mould issues, this product has been a lifesaver. It allows me to resolve mould problems quickly and efficiently. That is what keeps me writing well-thought out reviews, as your many QUALITY REVIEWS have been of GREAT BENEFIT to me again & again. Thank you. Now for my Review Of the compact KIDDE CARBON MONOXIDE ALARM that comes with a 7 year warranty. I was quite wary (i.e. unsure) about getting another Carbon Monoxide Alarm, as many reviews of Carbon Monoxide were either EXCELLENT, GLOWING REPORTS or very negative ones. So I decided to read a lot of the Carbon Monoxide Alarm Reviews and ANALYSE the results. (i.e. break down my understanding of what they all meant) The KIDDE Carbon Monoxide Alarm seemed to get a mix of both positive and negative feedback. However, having carefully considered its feedback, I decided it was worth considering. The Compact KIDDE CARBON MONOXIDE Alarm is indeed very compact weighing approx 200g (0.44 ounces) and its dimensions being Width * Length * Thickness ➡️ 7 * 12 * 3 cm ➡️ 2.76 * 4.72 * 1.18 inches. It hardly takes up any space and although it comes with screws to affix it on a wall or ceiling, it has a ready-made slot on the back of the alarm to enable you to hang it on a hook or nail that’s partly recessed into a wall. The Carbon Monoxide Alarm comes with instructions and Three “AA“ Size Batteries. It’s really easy to remove the cover to the battery compartment on the back of the Alarm. You just gently slide it down in the direction of the arrow and then put in the 3 * AA Batteries and then slide the compartment cover back on carefully. It’s important to note of course that it’s the actual Alarm Unit that comes with the 7 Year Warranty and NOT the batteries! You’ll probably need to change the batteries once every 7months to a year depending on HOW OFTEN the Carbon Monoxide Alarm sounds. [I say this as I’ve had a few KIDDE Carbon Monoxide Alarms in the past with at least two at any one time. Also, I believe that after about 5.5years or so, depending on HOW FREQUENTLY the Alarm goes off to alert you, the unit will need to be replaced as the CO Sensor inside the unit stops working!]. And VERY IMPORTANT: WHEN YOU FIRST PUT IN THE BATTERIES, THE CARBON MONOXIDE ALARM MAKES TEN RAPID BEEPS, WHICH STARTLED ME A BIT. I should have read the instructions that came with the unit more carefully. You’re also advised to write in the date ON THE BACK OF THE UNIT, the date you installed the Carbon Monoxide Alarm & the batteries, as both the Unit and the batteries have a LIMITED LIFE SPAN. I installed mine on Sunday 26 July 2020 and wrote that date on the Carbon Monoxide Unit. I think it would be easier to write down the installation date with a marker pen. AND REMEMBER to TEST the unit AT LEAST once a week and PREPARE for the loud 85 Decibel Screeching Sound. Some Carbon Monoxide Alarm Units require you to vacuum their insides once every two to three months. I LIKE IT THAT THIS UNIT DOES NOT APPEAR TO REQUIRE THIS! Some people have complained about their own Carbon Monoxide Alarms received being manufactured a few years before they received them. The two I received were MANUFACTURED ON NOVEMBER 9 2019. Thanks for Reading and Hope you’ve Found MY REVIEW HELPFUL... " Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Comfortable, True-to-Size Gloves That Don't Tear Easily I've tried quite a few disposable gloves over the years for various jobs, including DIY, maintenance work, and more 3D resin printing, and these have impressed me more than expected. Sizing is often an issue with disposable gloves, as many of the cheaper ones I've bought in the past tend to come up smaller than advertised. An XL can sometimes fit more like a Large. Thankfully, these are true to size. The XL fits me perfectly, with no tight spots and no excess material at the fingertips, making them comfortable to wear while still allowing good dexterity. The gloves strike a nice balance in thickness. They're not the thickest nitrile gloves I've used, but they're certainly not flimsy or paper-thin either. They provide a reassuring level of protection while still allowing enough finger sensitivity for detailed tasks. One thing I particularly like is how much stretch they have. They slide on easily and stretch well without immediately tearing, which is something I've experienced with cheaper gloves in the past. My main use for these has been 3D resin printing, where reliable hand protection is essential. During several printing sessions, I had no issues with resin penetrating the gloves, and they held up well while handling resin-coated parts. They gave me confidence that my hands were properly protected throughout the process. Being powder-free and latex-free is another plus, especially for anyone with latex sensitivities or who simply prefers gloves that don't leave residue behind. They're comfortable enough to wear for extended periods and don't have an overpowering chemical smell when first opened. Considering the fit, durability, comfort, and level of protection they provide, I think these offer excellent value for money. They perform exactly as I'd hoped and compare favourably with gloves that cost considerably more. Once this box is finished, I'll happily buy another. " Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Cost-Per-Hour Test Results & Unboxing Video Review After 8 Weeks of Use: Proaller Heated Electric Throw 160x130 cm I bought this recently based on the good reviews and reasonable price. I already have an electric blanket for the bed, and a couple of heat pads for myself and family (you can read my reviews for these by clicking on my account name above), and wanted to try something to use more casually for the chilly days ahead. It arrived vacuum-packed with an instruction booklet, and the cable/controller/mains plug already attached, ready to use. The fabric is 100% polyester on both sides, as confirmed on the sewn-in label. The coloured side is a velvety microfleece (often sold as “flannel”), while the white side that looks like wool is “sherpa” fleece, a knitted pile that mimics sheepskin. Flannel and sherpa are style names describing the texture, not the fibre, so neither side is actual wool, but polyester. However, both sides are incredibly soft, luxuriant, and warm even as a simple blanket when unheated. I measured the cable at just over 8 feet/ 2.5m in length overall, with the controller fixed along it about 2 feet from the blanket. It is connected by a small plastic unit bonded to one corner of the blanket. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. With the throw laid lengthways from chest to feet, with the white fleece side down, that connector will sit either by your right shoulder or by your left foot, depending on which way up you place it. If you want the controller within easy reach, you will probably choose the corner near your right shoulder. This can matter if your nearest mains socket is on the left, as the lead may then have to run across your chest or around your back, so it is worth bearing in mind. The controller is kept sensibly straightforward with just three buttons: • On/Off • Timer • Heat Some other brands try to add in special features with more buttons, which unnecessarily complicates things without actually giving any real benefits, especially if the person using it is not tech savvy or may have poor memory. The On/Off button is slightly concave, so it can be differentiated from the other two by touch, which is helpful in the dark, or for anyone with limited vision. The plastic screen over the display is slightly frosted, being clear enough to see the numbers, but reducing reflections, which is a good little detail. Once plugged into the mains, press the power button first. The display flashes for 10 seconds. If you do nothing, it switches itself off, so press either the temperature or timer button within that time to keep it on. On start-up, the default settings appear: temperature (red) 4 and timer (green) 3. The temperature runs from 1 to 9 and then H, so effectively H = 10, which is the warmest. The timer runs from 1 to 9, each number representing hours until auto-off. Each press increases the value and then cycles back to 1; you can adjust either setting at any time. After a change, the display flashes for about 5 seconds, then holds steady, and after another 5 seconds, it dims to roughly half brightness until you press a button again. This is good, as bright LEDs can sometimes be too harsh in a dark room. The green timer number counts down by one each hour to show the remaining time. There is no “Permanent On” option for safety reasons, but you can change or reset it whenever you like. If you switch off but leave the unit plugged in, your last settings are remembered for next time. If you unplug it, the settings revert to the defaults (temperature 4, timer 3) on the next start-up. Okay, now the interesting and important part: the actual cost of running it. Although the label states 150 W, that is the maximum “draw” when the element is on. In practice, most heated throws regulate warmth by cycling on and off, so the average power over an hour is usually much lower, particularly on the mid and low settings and will vary with room temperature etc. While this brand does not publish per-setting wattages or confirm the control method, this is how products of this type generally work, so I put it to the test. I have a plug-in power meter to measure the consumption of electrical devices, and sure enough it switches between 150 W to zero every few seconds, on and off. I ran a few tests on it at different heat settings and logged wattage / energy used over 60 minutes, and therefore the actual wattage and cost. Results (Per Hour): Heat No. _Watts __ Cost 1 _______ 29w___ 0.80p 3 _______ 35w___ 0.97p 5 _______ 46w ___ 1.27p 7 _______ 63w ___ 1.74p 10 (H) ___ 79w ___ 2.18p So, on medium (5) it costs just over 1 pence per hour in electricity, and on maximum heat 10 (H) a shade over 2p per hour. These figures are based on my energy provider and area, which is currently (at the time of writing, Oct 2025) 27.72p/kWh. Yours may vary slightly (you can check on your provider’s website), but roughly it means having the throw on a high setting for five hours in the evening will cost me about 11p, and on low about 4p. When switched on, the heat feels somewhere between a heat-pad and a standard electric blanket, but closer to the latter. On level 1 it is a touch above room temperature; at the maximum, H (used instead of 10 because the display only shows a single character), it is comfortably warm and sometimes too warm, but do not expect hot water bottle type temperatures. As with electric heated pads and blankets in general, it feels warmer where it is in contact with you. Sections that hang loosely at the sides lose more heat to the air and feel cooler than areas resting directly on the body. This can seem like an inconsistency at first, but it’s really just how heat behaves, so I took a photo with a thermal camera gadget I have (see attached picture), and the heating elements seem fairly consistent in temperature across the blanket. It is washable either by hand or machine. The instructions need to be read first, as this requires removing the cable. The plug which connects to the plastic socket, fixed to the blanket’s corner, has a button on either side which need to be squeezed then pulled apart. This needs some strength and wiggling as it’s a tight fit. It goes back in one way only, and is much easier to reconnect than pull apart. All good so far. -Pros: • Low power consumption, energy saving • Ultra soft material • Simple controller • Long cable • Hand and machine washable -Cons: • Connector needs some force to detach • Not suitable to lie or sit on Overall, this is pretty much what I was hoping for, and I don’t have any real criticisms. It’s soft, warm and cosy, and I’m definitely glad I bought it now that we’re heading towards winter. I’ve already avoided putting the living room fire on at times when I normally would, as this is enough when the room is just chilly. It makes me wonder how long it will be before it pays for itself, and then possibly moves into “credit” with heating bill savings? I would definitely recommend this to anyone looking for a new option to keep warm, and as a cosy treat for yourself or a loved one, so it’s five stars from me. The instructions for this hydrogel mask are incredibly clear, making the application process completely straightforward. On clean-shaven skin, like my girlfriend's face, the mask fits flawlessly with absolutely zero gaps. It hugs the contours of the face perfectly. Just keep in mind that this is a deep-treatment mask. It took about 3 to 4 hours to completely dry down, turn translucent, and absorb fully into the skin. The main challenge comes if you have a trimmed beard or facial hair. The hydrogel material cannot grip hair, so the lower half of the mask will not stick properly and tends to fall off. Only the upper section secured well to my forehead and upper cheeks.However, we found some great creative workarounds so nothing went to waste! My girlfriend applied the remaining jaw and chin section to my neck 😂, which worked beautifully. We also used the tiny punch-out eye and mouth patches creatively, placing the extra pieces above my eyebrows and using the mouth cutout across the bridge of my nose for targeted hydration. Pros:Truly delivers a noticeable boost in skin hydration and plumpness. Leaves the skin feeling incredibly smooth, refreshed, and deeply nourished. High-quality ingredients that genuinely work, offering great value for money. Cons: Not beard-friendly, as the lower half slides off facial hair. Requires 3–4 hours to dry, so it is best used when you have plenty of time or as an overnight mask. Final Verdict:If you have a smooth, clean-shaven face, this mask is an easy 5-star product because the fit and skin benefits are flawless. If you have a beard, the lower half simply won't stick. However, because it is highly effective and versatile enough to be repurposed on your neck and nose, it still deserves a solid 4 stars. Highly recommended, but beard wearers beware! In the event of the CO alarm sounding, follow these 3 steps: VENTILATE : Keep calm; open doors and windows to ventilate your home. Stop using fuel-burning appliances and turn them off. EVACUATE : Evacuate the property immediately. RING FOR HELP: If in the UK, call The National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If outside the UK, call your supplier's emergency number. Do not use appliances until they have been checked by an expert. Get medical help for anyone suffering the effects of CO poisoning. What are the symptoms of CO poisoning? Symptoms of CO poisoning include headache, dizziness, weakness, nausea and vomiting, rapid heartbeat, shortness of breath, seizures, chest pain, disorientation, and loss of consciousness. Who should I call in the event of a CO leak? If in the UK, call The National Gas Emergency Service on 0800 111 999. If outside the UK, call your supplier's emergency number. What are the sources of CO? The common sources of Carbon Monoxide (CO) are cookers, fires, boilers, oil and gas boilers, portable generators, oil or solid fuel cookers, gas or paraffin heaters, barbecues (BBQs), clogged chimneys, wood or gas fireplaces, cigarette smoke or any fossil fuel‑burning appliances. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. Started taking magnesium after reading about its role in sleep quality and muscle recovery, both areas that had been inconsistent for a while. Had tried a basic magnesium oxide supplement previously and abandoned it after a few weeks due to digestive discomfort that made daily use impractical. The glycinate, citrate and malate combination here is specifically formulated for better absorption and gentler digestion, which was the main reason for trying this version. The digestive side is considerably better. No cramping or discomfort even taken on an empty stomach, which with magnesium oxide had been an immediate problem. Taken in the evening as directed it sits without issue and has remained that way consistently throughout use. Sleep quality is where the most noticeable improvement showed up. Falling asleep felt easier within the first couple of weeks and the quality of sleep, specifically waking feeling more rested rather than just having logged the hours, improved in a way that felt meaningful rather than placebo. It's difficult to isolate a single supplement as the cause with complete certainty but the timing correlates closely enough to feel confident attributing at least part of the improvement to this. Muscle recovery after exercise also felt slightly better, less residual soreness after harder sessions, though this was a more subtle difference than the sleep improvement and harder to measure objectively. The 1800mg complex across three forms is a thoughtful formulation. Each form has slightly different absorption characteristics and the combination covers more bases than a single source supplement would. Falls just short of five stars on value alone, it's not the cheapest option in this category and reordering regularly adds up. But as a well formulated magnesium supplement that actually delivers without digestive compromise, it earns the repeat purchase. " Read more View Image Gallery Amazon Customer 5.0 out of 5 stars Images in this review Reviews with images See all photos Previous slide Next slide All photos Amazon Customer 5 out of 5 stars Decent Budget Gas I picked up this 8-pack of Straame gas for my portable single-burner stove, and honestly, the value is hard to beat. Gas canisters can be a total rip-off at local shops, so getting a bulk pack like this delivered is much easier on the wallet. The best thing about them is the overall performance for the price. They are standard bayonet-style cans, so once you line up the notch on the rim and lock the lever down, they work a treat. I was a bit worried they might be weak or sputter, but they produce a steady blue flame and handled cooking my breakfast without any drama. Each bottle seems to last just as long as the more expensive brands you find in camping stores, which was a nice surprise. The main annoyance is the metal collar on the top feels a tiny bit softer than the premium ones. You have to be careful when you are lining up the notch in the stove cradle, as you don't want to bend the rim or it won't seal properly. One thing to watch out for is that the safety lever on the front of the stove can be a bit stiff with these, so just double-check you have it sitting dead-centre before you force the lock down. If you are a camper or just someone who uses these single-burner stoves for a quick brew or a BBQ, these are an easy recommendation. They do exactly what they are supposed to do and keep the running costs right down. Full content visible, double tap to read brief content. So far, so good. I have had no trouble with the delivery; I think that, with an 8-pack, they were not able to roll around in the box. I have not used them - yet. I am feeling pessimistic about the oncoming winter months, and have invested in a camping stove and heater, as well as a couple of extra camping lanterns [these are USB rechargeable]. I used a stove years ago when rallying and needed some quick hot food, e.g. soup or even a fried egg sandwich. But now I am getting rather old and live on my own, and beginning to feel my age and realise, after a fall I had a few weeks ago, having to sit on a cold concrete floor for 6 hours waiting for an ambulance, that dear old Alexa was able to call for me [and she switched on the TV and even a small heater I had forgotten was linked to her]. I need more help than I was admitting to. But I like my independence, and these canisters can be used for items that will make my life easier if/when we have power cuts. The contents slide out of the sachets into the bowl, meaning you don't have to squash it out with your hands. The pieces of food look meatier than any other cat food brand, and there's just a fine layer of jelly. In the past, I've found my cats would eat the jelly and leave the meat. With these Felix sachets, they lick the dish clean. Each sachet holds the perfect amount to feed my three cats two sachets each a day. They have dried food too as they like a variety. Unlike other brands, there's barely any smell from this food. When I've put the food down at night and the cats go out without eating it, it doesn't dry up. They'll happily eat it when they come back in the morning. I rehomed a black cat whose fur was far from soft, but several months of eating Felix cat food shed got a lovely soft coat. None of my cats have ever been sick after eating Felix, unlike other food sachets which they were constantly throwing up. So it's obviously good for their digestion. One of my cats gets up onto my workbench and sits, staring at the cupboard. I keep the food in and won't budge until he's fed. That's him in the photo waiting on his food. I usually feed him separately as the two girls tend to budge in and eat his food too. My cats love it. They lick their dishes clean, and they'd definitely recommend it. For the last few years, my washing machine had been giving off the most horrendous smell after each wash, which I can only describe as an ungodly mix of sewage, garlic, and egg. It was absolutely disgusting, and the smell would spread throughout the house. I tried every solution I could think of, including bicarbonate of soda, vinegar, hot cycles, and even other chemical cleaners, but nothing worked. I cleaned every part of the machine, replaced the pipes, scrubbed the detergent drawer, cleaned the drip tray, and ran hot washes, but the smell just wouldn't go away. I was at my wit's end, especially with guests coming to stay, and I couldn’t bear the thought of them waking up to that awful odour. So, I scoured Amazon one last time and came across this Dr. Beckmann Service-it Deep Clean Washing Machine Cleaner. Its bold claims of removing 99.99% of bacteria, fungi, and viruses, as well as eliminating bad odours, seemed too good to be true, so I had to try it! All I can say is wow! Using it couldn’t be easier. Just empty the whole 250g box into the drum, no measuring required, and set your machine to run at a minimum of 60°C for at least an hour. I opted for a 90°C wash, which lasts for 2 hours on my machine, for extra thoroughness. After just one wash, the disgusting smell that had plagued my home for years was completely gone, and three weeks later, it still hasn’t returned. I’m absolutely amazed at how effective this product is. It left no mess, no residue, and it feels like I have a brand-new washing machine. For the price, it’s unbeatable. I paid £2.90 for the 250g pack, which is enough for one full clean, and I’ve seen the price drop lower. Given how effective it is, that’s an absolute bargain! I’ve already ordered a few more packs to use regularly, as it’s recommended to use every 1-2 months to keep your machine in top shape. The cleaner is supposed to leave a lemon fresh scent, though I didn’t really notice that. But honestly, the fact that my machine no longer smells at all is a win for me. Now all I can smell is my laundry detergent, and that’s good enough! I’ve tried a lot of other products, including well-known brands like Dettol, but none of them were able to tackle the odour like this. It also worked wonders on the limescale build-up in my 20-year-old machine, leaving the drum and seals sparkling clean. This cleaner is suitable for both front-loading and top-loading machines, and it’s great for prolonging the life of your appliance by preventing limescale and dirt build-up. If you’ve been dealing with an awful odour in your washing machine like I was, I can’t recommend this product enough. I wish I had found it sooner. It would have saved me so much frustration. I’ll definitely be using it regularly from now on, and I’m excited to try more from the Dr. Beckmann range. If you’re looking for a product that truly works and is great value for money, this is it!
